extraction_scope.notes: Worker-6 adjudicated mechanism strength from XML sections, figures, methods, and tables; unsupported LPS-affinity or exact molecular-target claims are not promoted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LBDv-His binds E. coli cells in an immunocytochemistry assay; this is direct bacterial-binding evidence, not a quantified LPS-binding constant.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding was shown for E. coli cells with His-tagged LBDv; the paper does not quantify binding affinity.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: LBDv against E. coli, Vibrio harveyi, and Staphylococcus epidermidis
mechanism_claims.claim_text: LBDv causes visible bacterial agglutination in the tested Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Agglutination is qualitative microscopy evidence and should not be generalized to untested species.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Scanning electron microscopy supports membrane/surface damage with cytoplasm leakage after LBDv treatment.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The evidence supports bacterial envelope disruption morphology; it is not a molecular target assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectra, structure-content calculations, and physicochemical parameters support beta-sheet-rich peptides with positive charge/amphipathicity as an indirect activity rationale.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The charge/amphipathicity statement is an inferred rationale and is not direct proof of a molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: LBDv in shrimp Vibrio harveyi challenge
mechanism_claims.claim_text: LBDv reduces recoverable V. harveyi colony counts in an in vivo shrimp challenge context.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports in vivo antimicrobial activity but is not a direct mechanistic assay.
